content.text:
I've read the challenge PDF, your CV/cover letter, and checked your machine (Python 3.12 via uv, Node 25, Docker + Compose, Tesseract 5 — no LLM API keys in the environment). `CLAUDE.md` with your rules is committed. Before I start building, here is my understanding and the decisions I need from you.

## What the challenge actually asks

Legal team's pain: **"which contracts do NOT contain passage X?"** and **"which contracts still use the old company name?"** across PDFs + JPEG scans of handwritten contracts on SharePoint. Deliverables: a pipeline that makes documents analyzable, a front-end, an end-to-end demo — plus a 15–20 min presentation later.

## Proposed design (what makes it different from "yet another RAG chat")

Plain RAG is good at finding *presence* and bad at proving *absence* — and absence is exactly what lawyers ask for. So at ingest time each contract is decomposed into **typed clauses** (liability cap, DPA/GDPR, termination, governing law, …) and **normalized parties/entities** with page + position. That gives:

- **"Missing passage"** → deterministic set-difference over a clause-coverage matrix, then an LLM *verifier* double-checks only the borderline cases with cited evidence (ties to your guardrails thesis).
- **"Company rename"** → exact entity hits with page coordinates → review queue → push approved copy to the (mocked) contract-storage REST API.
- **Model routing by document type:** born-digital PDF → pdfplumber, no LLM; scanned PDF → Tesseract, escalate to a vision model when confidence is low; handwritten JPEG → vision model directly. Cheap model for clause classification, strong model with thinking for verification.
- **Hybrid retrieval** (Postgres full-text + pgvector, RRF fusion) for free-form questions, every answer cited to contract/page/span.
- **Built-in eval:** since I generate the sample contracts, ground truth is known → precision/recall shown in the UI.

Stack (Riverty list ∩ your CV): Python 3.12 + FastAPI + LangGraph, Postgres/pgvector, React + TS + Vite, Docker Compose, small Terraform for Azure (Container Apps, PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Blob, Foundry) — not applied, for the infra story. pytest + Playwright.

Assumptions unless you say otherwise: UI and code in English; ~12 synthetic contracts (merchant/BNPL, DPA, NDA, vendor, debt-purchase), 2–3 of them in German; committing to `master` (the only branch).

questions.question: Which LLM provider/key can you provide? (I'll build an offline fallback in every case — Tesseract + deterministic stub — so the demo never depends on network.)

options.label: Google Gemini (Recommended)
options.description: Matches the challenge stack, strongest vision for handwritten JPEGs, free-tier key from AI Studio. Put GEMINI_API_KEY in .env.

options.label: Azure AI Foundry
options.description: Needs endpoint, key and deployment names for a chat + vision model and an embedding model.

options.label: Anthropic Claude
options.description: Not in Riverty's listed stack, but you already have access. Needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

options.label: No key — offline only
options.description: Tesseract OCR + stub LLM. Works, but no real reasoning/handwriting OCR in the demo.

questions.question: Do you confirm the core concept: clause-coverage matrix + entity registry at ingest, with an LLM verifier and RAG chat on top?

options.label: Yes, go with it (Recommended)
options.description: Absence detection becomes a deterministic query; LLM only verifies borderline cases and answers free-form questions.

options.label: Simpler: RAG chat + citations only
options.description: Standard vector RAG with cited answers. Less code, but 'which contracts lack X' relies on the LLM alone.

questions.question: For the sample data, may I use Riverty's real 2022 rebrand (Arvato Financial Solutions → Riverty) as the 'company name needs updating' scenario, with fictional counterparties?

options.label: Yes, use the real rebrand (Recommended)
options.description: Realistic and directly relevant to the interviewers; counterparties, people and amounts stay fictional.

options.label: Fully fictional names only
options.description: E.g. 'Nordbank Payments GmbH' → 'Nordpay'. Safer, less punchy.

questions.question: Frontend styling: use the MUI library itself, or Tailwind styled to look like Material?

options.label: MUI library (Recommended)
options.description: React + TypeScript + Vite + @mui/material. Clean Material look with minimal custom CSS.

options.label: Tailwind, Material-like
options.description: Matches your CV's Tailwind experience; more hand-written styling to get the Material feel.

## Current Gemini Models (2026)

Gemini has two families in 2026: Gemini 3 (3.1 Pro, 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash, Flash-Lite) and Gemini 2.5.

### Gemini 3 Series

**Latest Models:**
- Gemini 3.7 Flash (gemini-3.7-flash): Substantial improvements across software engineering, web development, and agentic workflows
- Gemini 3.6 Flash (gemini-3.6-flash): Features improved token efficiency and code/agentic planning capabilities at a lower price point than 3.5 Flash

### Thinking Capability

Gemini 3.5 Flash is based on the Gemini 3 Flash reasoning foundation with thinking levels to control the mix of quality, cost and latency. Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite will shut down on October 16, 2026 (Gemini Developer API) or October 20, 2026 (Agent Platform Gemini API).

# Gemini Thinking Model Support

Based on the documentation provided, here's a concise overview of thinking support across model families:

## Supported Models & Thinking Levels

**Gemini 3.x Series:**
- `gemini-3.7-flash`: Default medium thinking; supports `low, medium, high`
- `gemini-3.6-flash`: Default medium; supports `minimal, low, medium, high`
- `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`: Default minimal; supports `minimal, low, medium, high`
- `gemini-3.5-flash`: Default medium; supports `minimal, low, medium, high`
- `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`: Default high; supports `low, medium, high`
- `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image`: Default minimal; supports `minimal, high`
- `gemini-3-flash-preview`: Default high; supports `minimal, low, medium, high`
- `gemini-3-pro-preview`: Default high; supports `low, high`

**Gemini 2.5 Series:**
- `gemini-2.5-pro`: Enabled; supports `low, medium, high`
- `gemini-2.5-flash`: Enabled; supports `low, medium, high`
- `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`: Disabled by default; supports `low, medium, high`

## SDK Example

```python
interaction = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-3.7-flash",
    input="Your prompt here",
    generation_config={"thinking_level": "low"}
)
```

The `thinking_level` parameter accepts the values listed above depending on your chosen model.

cat > api/app/__init__.py <<'EOF'
EOF

cat > api/app/config.py <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=REPO_ROOT / ".env", extra="ignore")

    gemini_api_key: str = ""
    database_url: str = "REDACTED"
    data_dir: Path = REPO_ROOT / "data"

    # Model routing: reasoning effort follows the task, not the other way round.
    model_pro: str = "gemini-3.1-pro-preview"  # verification, handwriting OCR
    model_flash: str = "gemini-3.7-flash"  # classification, extraction, chat
    model_lite: str = "gemini-3.5-flash-lite"  # injection screening
    model_embedding: str = "gemini-embedding-001"
    embedding_dim: int = 768

    @property
    def llm_enabled(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.gemini_api_key)


settings = Settings()
EOF

cat > api/app/main.py <<'EOF'
from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.config import settings

app = FastAPI(title="Contract Intelligence API", version="0.1.0")


@app.get("/api/health")
def health() -> dict:
    return {"status": "ok"}


@app.get("/api/config")
def config() -> dict:
    return {
        "llm_enabled": settings.llm_enabled,
        "models": {
            "pro": settings.model_pro,
            "flash": settings.model_flash,
            "lite": settings.model_lite,
            "embedding": settings.model_embedding,
        },
    }
EOF

cat > api/Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-deu \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
WORKDIR /srv/api
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project
COPY app ./app
ENV PATH="/srv/api/.venv/bin:$PATH"
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
EOF

cat > web/Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM nginx:alpine
COPY --from=build /src/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
EOF

cat > web/nginx.conf <<'EOF'
server {
    listen 80;
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://api:8000/api/;
        proxy_read_timeout 300s;
    }
    location / {
        try_files $uri /index.html;
    }
}
EOF

cat > docker-compose.yml <<'EOF'
services:
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: contracts
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: contracts
      POSTGRES_DB: contracts
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U contracts"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  api:
    build: ./api
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
      GEMINI_API_KEY: ${GEMINI_API_KEY:-}
    volumes:
      - ./data:/srv/data:ro
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  web:
    build: ./web
    ports:
      - "5173:80"
    depends_on:
      - api

volumes:
  pgdata:
EOF

# pyproject: description + pytest config
sed -i '' 's/description = "Add your description here"/description = "Contract Intelligence API - Riverty RAG case study"/' api/pyproject.toml
cat >> api/pyproject.toml <<'EOF'

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
EOF
rm -f api/README.md; sed -i '' '/^readme = /d' api/pyproject.toml

# vite proxy
cat > web/vite.config.ts <<'EOF'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  server: {
    proxy: { '/api': 'http://localhost:8000' },
  },
})
EOF
echo done
